[h1][b]「魂の契約書にサインをしたな？ ならばアクセルを踏め。――バックミラーに映る『奴』から逃げ切る、深夜のオカルト・ドライブ」[/b][/h1]

[h1]ストーリー[/h1]
あなたは禁断の儀式を行い、悪魔と「取引」をして願いを叶えた。
だが、その代償は重かった。契約を破棄し、魂を救う唯一の方法は、老婆（The Crone）の待つ場所まで逃げ切ること。背後から迫りくる「何か」の気配を感じながら、あなたは終わりのない夜のハイウェイを疾走する。
ルールは一つ。止まってはいけない。家に帰るまでが遠足ではなく、家に帰るまでが「命がけ」だ。

[h1]概要[/h1]
PS1時代を彷彿とさせるローファイ（低解像度）な3Dグラフィックが特徴の、ホラー・ドライビングシミュレーター。

ジャンルとしては「ローグライク」に分類され、プレイするたびに道路状況やイベントが変化する。プレイヤーはハンドルを握り、アクセルとブレーキを調整しながら、同時に精神力（Sanity）と燃料を管理し、襲いかかる怪奇現象をアイテム（塩や聖水）で撃退しなければならない。

[h1]感想[/h1]
[b]深夜の運転中に感じる「ふとした不安」を、極限まで増幅させた悪夢。[/b]

このゲームが巧みなのは、ホラーの舞台を「車内」という閉鎖空間に限定したことだ。
雨の音、ワイパーの軋み、カーステレオからのノイズ。それら日常的な音が、精神力（SAN値）の低下とともに異常なものへと変貌していく。バックミラーをチラッと見た瞬間に「何か」が映ったり、道路標識が不吉な言葉に変わったりする演出は、派手さはないがジワジワと真綿で首を絞めるような怖さがある。

ゲームプレイは非常に忙しい。
ただ運転するだけではない。タバコを吸ってストレスを下げ、薬を飲み、地図を確認し、霊障が起きたら片手でハンドルを握りながらお祓いをする。この「マルチタスクのパニック感」こそが本作の醍醐味であり、焦りによって事故を起こした時の絶望感は筆舌に尽くしがたい。

レトロな画質が想像力を刺激し、見えないはずの恐怖を脳内で補完させる、雰囲気ゲーとしての完成度は非常に高い。

[h1]評価[/h1]
【GOOD】
・VHSテープのようなザラついた画質と、不気味なサウンドデザインが醸し出す、唯一無二の「呪われたゲーム」感。
・運転シミュレーターとホラー、そしてリソース管理を融合させた斬新なゲームシステム。
・1プレイは短いが、何度も死んで覚えるローグライク特有の中毒性と、ランダムイベントによるリプレイ性の高さ。

【BAD】
・[b]操作性の悪さと高難易度。[/b] 車の挙動が意図的にフワフワしており、少しのミスでスピンしやすい。それに加えて理不尽な即死イベントもあり、クリアするには運も必要。
・UIが見づらく、アイテムの使用やメニュー操作に慣れるまでは、恐怖よりも操作へのイライラが勝ることがある。
・説明不足な点が多く、何をすれば助かるのか分からないまま死に続ける「突き放した作り」は人を選ぶ。

Yeah, like everyone says, it's neat and moody but pretty shallow. I think there's an idea for a good game here, but I don't really want to play a non skill based driving game where I die a lot for no reason.

A pretty niche horror/driving-sim with very minimalist design that is effective at creating an oppressive atmosphere. 

Story is simple to the point of it barely being there but it works. You begin in a witches cabin discussing a ritual that will grant the player what ever they desire at a price. You simply type in your wish then begin the first half of the ritual after which you are sent to retrieve 3 items for the latter half. You set off in your car and the game begins.

Your car is driven with the WASD keys which feels kind of stiff but I found it fairly easy to adjust to after the first leg. It definitely feels like you're fighting to stay on the road at times but the spirit is definitely in the same vein as survival horror tank-controls. The twist is that the road changes depending on your mental state, driving is simple when you are mentally well taken care of but increasingly severe hallucinations begin to set in as your mental well being deteriorates. These hallucinations range from bits of gore occasionally dropping on the windshield to complete breaks from reality. It makes for some pretty tense moments in the rural backwater outside of the sporadic urban environments, especially when driving with damage and a dwindling fuel reserve.

Money can be earned picking up hitchhikers who occasionally appear on the side of the road. There's some nice sound design as their footfalls crunch in the gravel as they approach your car. They do little else than sit silently in the backseat and look menacing in the rear view but the presence of a scowling face staring back at you as you try to navigate the night is pretty off putting. 

Your main goal is pursued in the dozen or so cities on the map. Exploration is basic, you click on a list of locations to enter. You will mainly be upgrading your car and making repairs at the mechanics, seeking aid for your mental health in the form of medicine or cigarettes at the pharmacy or convenience store and purchasing one of the three objective items in the pawn shop. There are back alleys to explore that can yield some loot but I didn't engage with this much as it usually didn't turn out well for me. Basic as they are, the cities are a nice little break from driving and contribute to the atmosphere. The shopkeepers are all unfriendly and shrouded in shadow making the world feel just a tiny bit more hostile and the static images of skylines add a little diversity to the scenery after driving through the dark countryside and decaying outskirts.

Graphically it looks like a 5th gen console game with the jagged polygons and dithering. NPC's have a nice hand drawn look to them, making them pop out in the gritty interiors and the hallucinatory distortions that pop up during driving are effectively creepy and disturbing. Like everything else its simple and dirty in a way that benefits the experience.

There's some small complaints here and there, points where the players mental health seemed entirely drained regardless of how many drugs and cigarettes consumed and the random obstacles sometimes felt a little cheap. It can also run on the short end depending on your luck with which items spawn where (i'd say 30 minutes to an hour and a half has been my ballpark time to complete after 2 or 3 runs) and the ending is kind of predictably underwhelming. Regardless, its a gem and a pretty original horror experience.

The game is $3 my friend, so why are you reading this?! 3 dollars! I bought this game selling random trading cards I accrued through Steam play, and you could too. And yes... it's worth it. $3 dollars man. Get a job.

Okay seriously. It's a great little ride. If you however, like me, easily find yourself road raging in real life, well, take a chill pill before you load in, because some BS awaits. Okay, a lot of BS. People here can't drive. It's almost literally like driving through Kansas City, because people will forget what side of the road they drive on, there will be body parts flying out of a moving vehicle, and you'll get honked at constantly for things that are not your fault.

Every run is going to be slightly different. It's at it's best your first few time through when you really have no idea what's going to be happening to you. Enjoy those rides. I can't count the number of WTF moments when I first loaded this up. I was on edge, and really concerned that my character forgot to buckle the seat belt, because I knew I was as likely to crash as my drunk Uncle on the 4th of July. 

The money is tight... As tight as you are with yours. It's $3 Bucks man, why are you still reading this? I digress. You really have to be careful with your funds if your going to make it through. Even then, even when you're really trying, you might not have enough, because nothing is more horrifying then not having enough money for gas, a pack of cigarettes, AND your soul. It's a lot like real life with all this inflation. Still, you will start with more than $3 and have a decent chance of survival, just like you do right now.

The controls are easy to grasp and play with, and very very fun. It's so simple, yet extremely satisfying, or rage inducing, dependent upon how brutal the run is being on you. It's just a few buttons, but each one can save you're life, except maybe the button for the radio. Even when it's working right it's creepy. Who listens to that by choice?! It's clear the character was unhinged from the start.

Graphically, well... This is why you didn't spend the $3 isn't it?! Yeah, they are not great, but it adds to the charm, for me personally anyway. I actually enjoyed something that was more akin to the games I played way way back in the day. Lord knows there is as much BS in it too. It's all passable, and does what it's trying to do very well, and that's build tension, scare you, and make you start drinking to forget how awful of a driver you truly are.

The sound is GREAT. Again, so simple, yet so effective. The quiet is very quiet, and everything else, is very unnerving. The intro really sets the tone for what you're going to experience going forward, and remember, going forward is all you're going to do. There is no going back.

All and all a great little game. I highly recommend it, especially for your spooky season catalog of games. It's a really nice one to throw on come October. It's quick, entertaining, spooky, and ... only cost $3 dollars my dude.

Dead End Road is an unusual specimen, it's a hybrid horror game and arcade driving game.  Most of the gameplay has you driving a car around in the old Out Run/Test Drive/Pole Position style.  The roads aren't truly 3D, there a generated railroad that you steer slightly on to give you the impression you're playing a game.  This is weirdly married to a very poor, glitchy style horror adventure wrapper around the driving parts, and frankly, the hybrid doesn't work.  This isn't fun... it might be if the quality of the gameplay was better, but it's not. 

On the upside, the game does feature customisable controls and resolution, so at least some of the basic, minimum requirements have been met.  Unfortunately there's a number of other technical defects and shortcomings which contribute to the game being difficult to recommend to gamers.

There's an ugly screen filter meant to make the game look even more obsolete... like the game looks bad enough already, but they actually went out of their way to make it look worse.  There's no way to turn this off.

The graphics are all over the place, underneath the ugly filter.  Some pixel "art" (ugh), some low poly stuff, then some maybe okay looking assets for the rest of the game.  It's a little bit like the graphics have multiple personality disorder... regardless, this cludging is the kind of thing that's going to dissuade gamers from wanting to play the game.  Absolutely, there's no cutting edge visuals here, the game looks bad. 

The game never really caught on with the millions of gamers on Steam, with a very low peak player count close to launch, and then just a handful of players launching this game every couple of days.  This is undoubtedly caused by factors such as those raised in this review.  It's always helpful with buying decisions to consider how popular and successful the product is, and unfortunately while this did accumulate a few participation trophy reviews, overall, people just aren't using it.

The game contains stock/store assets/libraries/packages, but the "developer" here hasn't credited the people who actually did the work for the game.  An example is the non-commercial "Window wiper" sound that's copyrighted by RobinHood76.  In some cases this breaches the license agreement the developer signed for the use of those assets.  Worse, some of the assets are licensed under a [b]NON-COMMERCIAL AGREEMENT[/b], but the developer is violating those licenses [b]FOR PROFIT[/b].  The copyright holders deny permission to use their assets in paid products, which is what the developer has done here.  This is not just a contractual/license breach, in many jurisdictions this is a breach of criminal law.  Claiming credit for the work of others as well as breaching software licenses and breaking the law is highly unethical.

So, should you buy this game?

Dead End Road is relatively cheap at $3 USD, but it's not worth it. Given the defects and quality issues with the game, coupled with the unrealistic price, and the questionable ethical nature of the developer and/or their associates (as outlined above), this is impossible to recommend.  Remember that if you buy a game from an unethical developer, you're putting your money at risk.

Игра очень неоднозначная, по стилю и атмосфере шикарно получилось, особенно приятно, что скримеров реально мало, в основном игра нагнетает атмосферу.
А теперь главный минус игры: она максимально нечестная по отношению к игроку. Мало того, что управление достаточно дурацкое, так еще и многие препятствия на дороге генерятся так, что иногда невозможно объехать всё, не получив при этом урона, а он копится очень быстро. Даже подбирая всех попутчиков на своем пути и проходя почти что без урона, ты сливаешь кучу денег на врача, потому что уровень стресса персонажа накапливается ОЧЕНЬ быстро (причем по непонятным порой причинам, иногда вроде получаешь урон и видишь всякую нёх, но стресс остается низким, а иногда едешь идеально тот же самый кусок и ловишь dangerously high level), а дешевые успокоительные не помогают вообще, если стресс высокий (нет, это не преувеличение, они абсолютно бесполезны). За игру встречаешь 3-4 попутчиков, с каждого по 15 баксов которые тут же улетают на починку, лечение кукухи и предметы, в итоге ты - нервный нищеброд на убитой копейке, потому что всё равно ни на что не хватило. [h1]So you've finally arrived, my dear.[/h1]
[i]Dead End Road[/i] is a bit less than it seems to be. On first glance, it is a randomly generated cross-country adventure as you escape demons who are hot on your heels, eager to destroy you for daring to summon them in the first place. In actuality, [i]Dead End Road[/i] is a bit more predictable than that. Once you figure out you've got a map, routes can be plotted. And as you die and realize the roads don't change, the town names stay the same, and the shops within those towns also remain the same, [i]Dead End Road[/i] feels... tamed. 

But this is to underestimate what is a fun and engaging, even novel, horror game. The game starts you with one hundred pounds, and two core objectives. The first is to gather a bell, a candle, and a book with which you can undertake the ritual. The second is to reach the eponymous Dead End Road. But the game is balanced meticulously. Things are never that simple. Stress gets to you - hallucinations on the road become more and more grave. Things start to spiral out of control the longer you go without buying stress-relieving drugs. Then there's your poor car to consider. 

It gets beat up out there on those roads, dodging oncoming traffic, bumbling over pot holes, and crashing into spectral figures that practically throw themselves in front of your car. Both your own health and the vehicle's health are crucial considerations - and wonderful ones, at that. The game is a tightrope walk to the end, rewarding both skilled play and encouraging replayability as you slowly map out strategies to reach the end. 

It might not be particularly scary, but it can be a little unsettling, and I think mostly it's just very clever and does what it sets out to do. It's a horror driving simulator, and it simulates a desperate drive through the night, through the lashing rain, and does it very well. Highly recommended if you're in the mood for some bite-sized horror.

[h1] Short Review[/h1] 

Oh man I love horror games, especially those with weird concepts that aren’t walking simulators. This one is different, it’s a driving simulator. Also, PS1 style graphics. What wouldn’t I love about it?
A lot. To be honest I really liked the games premise, you commit a ritual and in order to finish it you need to write a thing you want, including an answer giving you a secret second ending and 3 items. 

You don’t know what you’re doing is alright and which way to go as you get presented multiple choices, from going into the dark alleyway to upgrading your car or buying cigarettes to reduce your stress level. Should I drive left for city x or right to city y? When I need to get a bell, is a broken one okay too?

Soundtrack, the mix between MIDI sound effects and normal ones, while sometimes you hear distorted voices coming from the radio which speak English but are hard to understand give a real unique vibe.

Then there are obviously the trippy sequences during the driving part, which will get you by surprise. Now why I don’t recommend the game? It’s the length and the driving aspect. One playthrough takes you 20 minutes or more, but the thing is that a single crash means a full reset to the beginning of the game. Which can happen easily due to the sudden appearances of other cars. Also, it’s in the UK therefore you drive on the wrong side of the road.

Also, it’s the driving. Oh god the driving is so atrocious. To steer left or right you must drive almost come to a standstill as when you drive normal speeds you can steer completely to one direction but will solely negate the natural drift the game imposes on you. You will drive either left or right very quickly when not completely counter steering. This type of driving was just not for me and therefore I don’t recommend it.

Dead End Road, a horror based driving game where you preform a ritual to grant one single wish with the dark powers. I loved playing through this game. It can seem unfair and brutal to begin with, but once you learn to drive slow and cautiously, spend your money wisely, plan your route to use the petrol stations to save money on buying fuel, it becomes much more bearable. There is a fair amount of RNG to whether you get the required items, but the game is not as strict on the items as you may think, just make sure you have a decent book, candle and bell and you should be fine. After multiple playthroughs I've only had one run fail because the game didn't have a candle in any of the shops on my planned route I always use.
